nodes.description: This allele-class branch applies when biallelic nonsense, frameshift, or other loss-of-function variants prevent production of a functional VDR protein. Loss of the receptor abolishes both ligand-activated transcription and the ligand-independent receptor function needed for hair cycling.

genetic_context.description: This branch is one alternative VDR defect and is not asserted for every affected individual.

nodes.description: Scalp and body alopecia often develops after initially normal hair. It is a strong diagnostic clue but is absent in a substantial minority and varies by the functional class of the VDR variant.

Ligand-affinity and coactivator-recruitment defects can preserve this branch, explaining why alopecia is genotype dependent and absent in some affected individuals.

nodes.description: Calcitriol synthesis remains intact while mineral deficiency, secondary hyperparathyroidism, and dysregulated receptor-mediated vitamin D homeostasis favor a markedly elevated circulating 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D concentration. nodes.description: High-dose oral elemental calcium is an initial bypass strategy when it can restore normocalcemia and suppress secondary hyperparathyroidism. It may also permit transition away from intravenous calcium, but passive absorption is limited and requires close biochemical and urinary-calcium monitoring.

A rescue experiment that separates the two arms of the disorder. Restoring a receptor that cannot bind hormone, in keratinocytes only, restores normal hair cycling, showing that the hair-follicle function of the receptor is ligand independent. As a transgenic mouse rescue, it does not establish universal treatment nonresponse of alopecia across human VDDR2A genotypes.

Mice develop severe undermineralized short bones and dysmorphic growth plates. This is an allele-mechanism model rather than a generic proxy for all VDDR2A: its phenotype is more severe than Vdr null and is not corrected by the high-calcium/phosphate/lactose rescue diet that normalizes the null model.
